# Verifiable Practice

Verifiable Practice (VP) is a **full project quality management system for human–AI collaboration**. It defines how a project establishes its goals and authority, plans controlled work, makes justified choices, verifies results, keeps an auditable history, accepts deliverables and maintains their justification over time.

Falsification and honest reporting provide its evidence discipline. Project roles, stage gates, records, independent assessment and revalidation turn that discipline into a repeatable management method. VP applies to code, specifications, documents, experiments and other maintained project artefacts.

The method uses Markdown documents and directories. No specialised software, database, service or persistent AI team is required. This repository also packages the method as a reusable AI skill: [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) gives operating rules and routes an assistant to the references needed for its current responsibility.

## Start Here

- **Understand the complete method:** read [How VP Works](docs/how-vp-works.md), then [Why VP](WHY.md) for its motivation and evidence discipline.
- **Start or adopt a project:** use [Project Planning and Records](playbooks/project-records.md), the [standard](standards/project-records.md) and [templates](templates/project-records/README.md).
- **Give an AI working instructions:** provide [SKILL.md](SKILL.md), the project's charter and its current task. Keep owner, worker and assessor responsibilities explicit.
- **Resume a project:** read its `PROJECT.md`, `PLAN.md`, `STATE.md`, `LEDGER.md` and `COVERAGE.md`; check source identity, open work, deadlines and triggers before proceeding.
- **Learn the foundations:** use the concept sequence below. A bounded task loads the references relevant to that task.
headings: Using VP with Any AI Tool

# Verifiable Practice

VP is a full project quality management system for human–AI collaboration. Its epistemology supplies evidence discipline; its owner/worker/auditor roles, controlled stages, quality criteria, records and review gates manage the complete project lifecycle. This skill distributes and routes the method.

legacy history is not certified and a conformance claim needs independent A.
These repository-specific links do not enrol another project using this skill.

Treat every material claim as something that must be possible to check. Establish what the user is trying to achieve, identify what would show the current approach is wrong, seek that evidence, and report the observed result—including failures and uncertainty.

# Why Verifiable Practice

Verifiable Practice (VP) is a **full project quality management system for human–AI collaboration**. It manages the work from the originating goal and mandate through planning, implementation, quality checks, acceptance, maintenance and retirement. Its records let another person or AI inspect the choices and evidence that justify the work.

Human and AI contributors need shared criteria, bounded authority and continuity across sessions. Falsification gives them a way to challenge technical claims. Project management supplies the roles, stages, gates and durable history needed to act on that evidence.

Bullshit is not lying. Liars know the truth and conceal it. Bullshitters are indifferent to truth. They say what sounds right, what fits the meeting, what satisfies the prompt. Whether it happens to be true is incidental.

Software engineering is drowning in bullshit. "Best practice" that nobody tested. Architecture decisions justified by vibes. AI-generated code that looks correct and compiles and passes the obvious tests and fails in production.

VP makes goals, choices, quality criteria, evidence and acceptance decisions explicit and reviewable.

## Why a Project Needs the Whole Method

A good test is one part of a continuing project. Someone must decide what outcome matters, what work is authorised, how much uncertainty and cost are acceptable, which result justifies a choice, and when changed conditions require review. Those decisions must remain understandable after the original conversation disappears. Owned manifests explain retained inputs, byte identities, custody and retention; independent copies support recovery. Missing old history remains unknown, while new choices and evidence justify current work.
headings: Why a Project Needs the Whole Method

# Bullshit Detection

Honest reporting supports quality control and independent assurance in [VP's project quality management system](../docs/how-vp-works.md). Records preserve failures, uncertainty and rejected choices alongside successes.

Bullshit is not lying. Lying requires knowing the truth and choosing to contradict it. Bullshit is indifference to truth - saying what sounds good without caring whether it is accurate.

AI systems bullshit constantly. They are trained to please. RLHF optimises for human satisfaction, not factual accuracy. Given ten results - nine good, one catastrophic - the system learns to emphasise the nine and bury the one.

Humans bullshit for the same reason. We do not like bad news. We reward the messenger who sanitises.

## The Problem

"The engine works nine times out of ten" is bullshit. It sounds like information but contains none. What matters is:

- When does it fail?
- What conditions distinguish success from failure?

# Engineering Standards: A Verification-First Approach

Engineering standards provide product-quality criteria within [VP's project quality management system](../docs/how-vp-works.md). Authorised changes, verification records and acceptance gates connect implementation checks to the project goal.

> This document is the canonical engineering standards reference for Verifiable Practice.

## Philosophy and Principles

This document defines engineering standards built on a fundamental insight: **safety comes from verbs, not nouns**. Correctness emerges from actions — checking, validating, asserting, testing, monitoring — not from static structures like type systems or design patterns. The act of verification matters more than the classification system.

### Core Tenets

- **Falsifiability as Foundation**: You cannot prove code correct, but you CAN prove it wrong. A single counterexample demolishes a claim. Tests should try to break code, not confirm it works. "All tests pass" provides weak confidence; "I tried hard to break it and failed" provides strong confidence.
- **Verbs Over Nouns**: Correctness comes from actions, not classifications. "This value was validated" matters more than "this has type ValidatedInput". The verb happened or it didn't. The assertion passed or it failed. That's provable.
- **Types Are Hints, Not Guarantees**: Type systems are incomplete — they cannot express "this list is sorted" or "this connection is authenticated". Types constrain design toward what the checker can verify, not what the problem demands. Use types as documentation, but rely on assertions and invariants for correctness.
- **Test the Real System**: Mocks hide integration failures. Real systems have real network latency, real concurrency, real resource contention, real failure modes. Integration-first testing, with targeted unit tests only for complex isolated logic.

# Falsifiability

Falsifiability supplies the evidence discipline for empirical claims in [VP's project quality management system](../docs/how-vp-works.md). Protocols, identified attempts and review triggers make that discipline auditable.

You cannot prove code correct. You can prove it wrong.

A single counterexample demolishes a claim. A thousand passing tests merely fail to falsify. This asymmetry is not a limitation - it is the only epistemically honest stance available.

## The Contract

An empirical claim relied on by a project choice carries three obligations:

1. I can articulate what would prove me wrong
2. I have tried to find that counterexample
3. I am reporting actual confidence, not performing confidence

# Goals

Goals establish continuing value and owner authority in [VP's project quality management system](../docs/how-vp-works.md). The charter, stages and acceptance decisions keep technical work connected to the originating mandate.

Everything else exists because of this.

The pillars - falsifiability, rhetoric, verification, all of it - are means. Goals are the end. Without clarity on what we are trying to achieve, rigorous method is just expensive wandering.

## Terminal and Instrumental

A **terminal goal** is what we actually want. An **instrumental goal** is a step toward it.

Confusion between the two is the root of most project failure. We optimise an instrumental goal until it consumes all resources, forgetting it was supposed to serve something larger. The test suite passes, but the product is useless. The architecture is elegant, but it solves the wrong problem.

The question is always: what does this serve?

# Precise Technical English (PTE)

Precise contracts make requirements and acceptance criteria checkable within [VP's project quality management system](../docs/how-vp-works.md). Use precision where ambiguity changes project choices or outcomes.

Natural language fails at precision. Not because English lacks expressive power, but because it optimises for the wrong thing: speaker economy. Humans compress. They rely on context, shared assumptions, and the listener's willingness to infer. This works in conversation. It fails in specifications.

PTE is a constrained subset of English designed for one purpose: eliminating ambiguity in technical communication. It is verbose, tedious, and unnatural. These are features. The goal is mutual intelligibility when precision is non-negotiable.

## Why PTE Exists

Consider: "The service calls the API. It fails."

Which failed? The service? The API? The call? Natural English does not say. The reader guesses. The guess becomes an assumption. The assumption becomes code. Sometimes the code is wrong.

This is not an edge case. Every specification contains dozens of such ambiguities:

# Rhetoric

This concept helps collaborators distinguish evidence, values and authority when making choices within [VP's project quality management system](../docs/how-vp-works.md). Decisions preserve those distinctions and their sources.

Aristotle proposed three modes of persuasion: Ethos (authority), Pathos (what people want), Logos (logic). Most engineers believe they operate purely in Logos. They are mistaken.

## The Hidden Pathos

The logical requirements of any system are an attempt to meet the emotional requirements of the people paying for it. By not being explicit about this, we create constant misalignment between the real world - "I need to please my client" - and the imagined logical world - "I need to please the type checker."

Logic is tautologically correct. It has no truth value outside itself. When we attempt purely logical work, we smuggle in Pathos - a moral or aesthetic motivation - to convert the tautology into something externalisable.

When someone insists that functional programming is "cleaner" or a particular architecture is "more elegant," they are making Pathos claims dressed in Logos clothing. There is nothing wrong with this. But call it what it is.

## The Ethos Problem

# The Verification Cycle

The verification cycle governs implementation steps within [VP's full project quality management lifecycle](../docs/how-vp-works.md). Project authority, stages, records and gates supply its surrounding controls.

Safety comes from verbs, not nouns. Correctness emerges from actions - checking, validating, asserting, testing - not from static structures like type systems or design patterns.

"This value was validated" matters. "This has type ValidatedInput" does not, unless validation actually occurred. The verb happened or it did not. That is provable.

## The Cycle

```
Design → Plan → Deconstruct → [Test → Code → Document] → Next
```

Each phase has entry and exit criteria. Skipping phases is not speed; it is debt with compound interest.

# The Zero-Code Contract

The zero-code contract is one software-delivery arrangement within [VP's full project quality management system](../docs/how-vp-works.md). It is useful when an AI can produce implementation faster than a human owner can review every line. The human focuses on criteria and evidence while the AI performs authorised implementation.

Projects can agree other allocations of human and AI technical work. Owner, worker, record keeping and independent-assessor responsibilities still need explicit mandates and boundaries.

If the human must review all code, the human becomes the bottleneck. Bottlenecks get bypassed. "Looks good" becomes the path of least resistance. Quality collapses.

## The Roles

The table below describes the **default human-owner arrangement** for this zero-code pattern. For an
AI owner, use the explicit [mandate and role contract](../standards/project-records.md)
and [independent audit roles](../docs/independent-record-audit.md). An AI owner
may make delegated management decisions; the working AI still implements and
maintains records. An actor title never creates authority, and the auditor
must remain independent of the authors it assesses.

# Document Work

Document analysis, planning and description provide content-quality control within [VP's full project quality management method](how-vp-works.md). Record document requirements, sources, changes and evidence under the project's authority and acceptance gates.

VP treats documents as instruments: they should change a reader's understanding, decision, or action. Three related modes address different failures.

| Mode | Question | Use it when |
|------|----------|-------------|
| Analysis | What does this document claim, optimise, and cause? | Something feels wrong or unsupported |
| Planning | What must this document accomplish, for whom? | An important document has not yet been drafted |
| Description | What model will let this reader understand the thing? | The subject is understood but difficult to explain |

## Analysis

Analysis separates direct statements from interpretation. It extracts stated goals, examines incentives and effects, identifies rhetorical modes, tests important claims for falsifiability, and shows the gap between what is promised and what is optimised.

# How Verifiable Practice Works

Verifiable Practice (VP) is a **full project quality management system for human–AI collaboration**. It combines project governance and planning, evidence-based technical work, durable decision/artefact records, independent assurance, controlled acceptance and continuing revalidation.

The system covers a project from its originating goal to maintenance, recovery and retirement. Code, specifications, documents and experiments use the same management and traceability principles. Falsifiability and honest reporting are its epistemic foundation; roles, controls and records make those principles operational across sessions and contributors.

## What the System Manages

| Quality function | Required project work | Where VP defines it |
|------------------|-----------------------|---------------------|
| Planning | Goal and mandate, scope, requirements, acceptance/harm criteria, responsibilities, risks, stages, budgets and tolerances | [Project standard §4](../standards/project-records.md), [project playbook](../playbooks/project-records.md), [templates](../templates/project-records/README.md) |
| Control | Test important claims, inspect artefacts against their contracts, preserve inputs/results and contain failed or unsupported work | [Verification cycle](../concepts/verification-cycle.md), [engineering standards](../concepts/engineering-standards.md), [investigation](../playbooks/investigation.md), [document analysis](../playbooks/document-analysis.md) |
| Assurance | Independently assess records, evidence support, traceability and current validity; respond to findings and check closure | [Project Audit](../playbooks/record-audit.md), [independent role guide](independent-record-audit.md), standard §11 |
| Improvement | Use failures, audit findings, invalidated premises and process-cost observations to revise choices and the method | [Reasoning review](../playbooks/review.md), standard §§7/10–12, [behaviour evaluation](testing-ai-behaviour.md) |

Quality management ties these activities to continuing project value and accountable acceptance. A passing test has a scope; a manager's authority has a mandate; a record-conformance verdict has a snapshot and time. Each needs the appropriate evidence or authorisation.

# Project Planning and Records

Project planning, control and traceable records are the management layer of [VP's full project quality management system](how-vp-works.md). They connect the owner mandate and quality criteria to bounded stages, choices, implementation evidence, independent gates and continuing review. The working AI keeps the records under owner oversight; an independent assessor checks their support.

A project can span many sessions, builds, contributors and machines. A status summary alone rarely explains what an earlier author knew, which alternatives failed, which exact binary produced a result or whether a premise remains current.

The [standard](../standards/project-records.md) supplies that implementation.
It is the explicit planning/record-conformance contract, version 1.0 proposed for adoption; the other VP procedures supply engineering, document and investigation quality checks.
Use the [playbook](../playbooks/project-records.md) for actions and the
[templates](../templates/project-records/README.md) for files.

The [independent audit loop](independent-record-audit.md) separates an assessor
from the working AI: a frozen packet leads to sourced findings, worker
responses and a fresh closure audit. The assessor stays within record
verification while the worker performs authorised technical investigation.

# Review and Audit

Review, product-quality assessment and independent record assurance are distinct controls within [VP's full project quality management method](how-vp-works.md). Their scopes and evidence feed owner acceptance and improvement decisions.

VP has two audit kinds: **Project Audit** (`project`) and **Code Audit**
(`code`). “Independent record audit” is another name for Project Audit.
Reasoning review is a separate, lighter activity.

For “Please audit X” or another ambiguous request, the AI must ask which kind
is intended and wait before starting. A charter default or the contents of X
must not silently choose it. Use [Audit Routing](../playbooks/audit-routing.md).

| Dimension | Project Audit | Code Audit | Reasoning review |
|-----------|---------------|------------|------------------|
| Subject | Plans, decisions, records, provenance, validity and code-to-root traceability | Implementation and executable contracts | Current reasoning and goal alignment |
| Finds | Missing/unreliable history, unsupported reliance, expired claims and record gaps | Defects, silent failures, missing technical validation | Drift, weak falsifiers, selective reporting |
headings: Why Audit and Repair Are Separate

# Skill Architecture

Verifiable Practice is a full project quality management system for human–AI collaboration, distributed as a self-contained skill repository. The [method overview](how-vp-works.md) explains governance, planning, quality control/assurance, acceptance and maintenance. This architecture separates discovery, procedures, normative contracts, templates and actual project records so an AI loads the references needed for its role and task.

## Repository Layers

```text
verifiable-practice/
|-- SKILL.md       Skill metadata, shared rules, and routing
|-- concepts/      Stable reasoning principles
|-- playbooks/     Operational procedures for particular tasks
|-- docs/          Explanation for human and AI readers
|-- standards/     Normative contracts for explicitly adopted practices
|-- templates/     Copyable Markdown documents and record fields
|-- vp/            This project's instantiated charter, records and evidence
|-- README.md      Project entry point

# Select the Audit Kind

Use this entry point whenever an owner asks for a VP audit. Select its kind
before loading an audit procedure or inspecting the project as an audit.

| Kind | Canonical name | Subject | Procedure |
|------|----------------|---------|-----------|
| `project` | Project Audit | Goal/plan/decision history, records, provenance, evidence support, validity, custody and code-to-root traceability | [Project Audit](record-audit.md) |
| `code` | Code Audit | Implementation defects, engineering standards, executable contracts and missing technical checks | [Code Audit](code-audit.md) |

“Record audit”, “independent record audit” and “project conformance audit” are
aliases for Project Audit. A short [reasoning review](review.md) is a separate
review activity; it is not a substitute for either declared audit.

## Mandatory Clarification

# Code Audit

Audit a codebase against the [engineering standards](../concepts/engineering-standards.md), produce a prioritised report, and—only when authorised—repair violations with adversarial tests.

Auditing and fixing are separate decisions. A request to inspect code authorises a report, not source changes.

**Audit kind:** `code`. Use this only after an explicit kind has been selected
through [Audit Routing](audit-routing.md). For an ambiguous “Please audit X”,
ask the intended kind and wait before inspecting. Project-record conformance
uses [Project Audit](record-audit.md) with a separate assessor contract.

## Phase 1: Scope

1. Identify languages, source roots, test commands, generated code, vendored code, and build artefacts.
2. Exclude trivial re-export files unless they contain behaviour.
3. Record the exact file set and exclusions in the report.

# Hypothesis-Driven Debugging

Use a debugger as a measurement instrument. State the hypothesis and its falsifier before issuing commands.

## 1. Verify the Subject

Before attaching a debugger, prove that the executable and symbols correspond to the source under investigation. Record an identifier such as a build ID, checksum, timestamp relationship, or reproducible build reference. If the executable is stale or provenance is uncertain, rebuild before drawing conclusions.

Also record the invocation, environment, inputs, and configuration needed to reproduce the fault.

## 2. State Competing Hypotheses

Write at least two plausible explanations when possible. For each one state:

- what you believe is happening;
- the exact observation that would contradict it;

# Project Discovery

Discovery is a collaborative, read-only process for understanding a project whose artefacts, history, goals, or value are unclear. It produces a durable report for recovery; it does not reorganise the project.

## Phase 1: Establish Context

Ask the user what the project was trying to achieve, when the work occurred, where related artefacts may exist, what outcomes matter, and what they remember as false starts. Their memory supplies intent that files cannot establish.

Do not treat memory as proof of technical behaviour. Treat it as primary evidence of purpose and value, then verify technical claims against artefacts where possible.

## Phase 2: Archaeology

For each agreed location:

1. inventory what exists without changing it;
2. identify likely relevance from names, dates, version history, and small metadata reads;

# Document Analysis

Analyse a document, proposal, idea, or communication by separating what it says from what it rewards or causes.

## Process

1. Acquire the complete target and establish its provenance, audience, date, and context.
2. Read [Goals](../concepts/goals.md), [Rhetoric](../concepts/rhetoric.md), [Bullshit Detection](../concepts/bullshit-detection.md), and [Falsifiability](../concepts/falsifiability.md).
3. Extract stated goals using direct quotations.
4. Infer actual goals from incentives, resource allocation, requested actions, omissions, and who benefits.
5. Separate Ethos, Pathos, and Logos. Identify where one is presented as another.
6. List consequential claims and the evidence that would falsify each one.
7. Compare stated and actual goals. Explain the practical consequence of any gap.
8. Invite correction where intent cannot be established from the document.

## Output

# Document Description

Help a user describe a system, codebase, process, or concept they understand but have not yet expressed clearly.

## Process

1. Establish what is being described and inspect it when source material is available.
2. Identify the exact audience and the decision or task the description must enable.
3. Ask for the three facts the audience must understand.
4. Identify common misconceptions and confusing boundaries.
5. Surface inputs, outputs, state changes, dependencies, failure modes, and non-goals as applicable.
6. Test possible analogies. State where each analogy breaks.
7. Propose an outline, then draft only after the user confirms the model.
8. Check the draft against the real system and the stated reader outcome.

## Suggested Structure

# Document Planning

Plan an important document before drafting it. The goal is agreement about the outcome, reader, evidence, and structure—not premature prose.

## Process

Work through these questions with the user:

1. **Document type:** What is being written, and what decision or action surrounds it?
2. **Terminal goal:** What should be different after the intended reader reads it?
3. **Audience:** Who exactly will read it? What do they know, value, fear, and control?
4. **Evidence:** Which claims require support, and what sources are authoritative for each?
5. **Failure:** What reader response would show that the document failed?
6. **Constraints:** Length, tone, format, deadline, review process, and required sections.
7. **Structure:** What sequence gives the reader the context needed for each conclusion?

# Investigation

Use this playbook for a focused question that can be answered by experiment. An investigation produces evidence, not a feature.

## 1. State the Hypothesis

Turn the concern into one specific, testable claim. Confirm with the user:

- the hypothesis;
- the observation that would falsify it;
- the practical decision the result will inform.

Do not experiment until these are clear.

## 2. Isolate the Work

# Precise Technical English

Use this playbook to turn ambiguous requirements into falsifiable technical statements. Read [Precise Technical English](../concepts/pte.md) first.

## Activation

Apply PTE only where ambiguity is costly: interfaces, invariants, state transitions, preconditions, postconditions, failure behaviour, security boundaries, and acceptance criteria. Use natural prose for rationale and explanation.

## Resolution Loop

1. Render the current understanding as explicit condition-action statements.
2. Identify the one unresolved ambiguity that most affects implementation or verification.
3. Ask one focused question.
4. Record the answer as a requirement clause.
5. Repeat until each material clause has one testable interpretation.

# Project Planning and Records

Use when establishing VP record conformance, planning a conformant project,
or working inside one that has already adopted the
[standard](../standards/project-records.md). Templates are
[here](../templates/project-records/README.md). This playbook implements the
standard; it does not grant authority to migrate, delete, publish or release.

# Project Recovery

Recovery restructures a project after discovery while preserving valuable outcomes. It is the action phase; use a verified discovery report whenever one exists.

## 1. Load the Evidence

Read the discovery report. Confirm with the user whether anything has changed and whether any verdict has been reconsidered. If no report exists, explain the risk and perform discovery first unless the user explicitly chooses a narrower recovery based on current evidence.

## 2. Plan Reversible Steps

For each step record:

| Field | Requirement |
|-------|-------------|
| Action | One precise filesystem or documentation change |
| Reason | Link to the discovery finding it serves |

# VP Project Planning and Records Standard

**Version:** 1.0, proposed 19 October 2026.

This is the normative standard for a project declaring conformance to VP
project planning and records. “Must” is required for conformance; “should”
allows a documented reason for another approach; “may” is optional.
Ordinary use of VP does not itself declare this conformance.

In this standard, **Project Audit** (kind `project`) means independent
assessment of project records, choices and justification. “Record audit” is
an alias. **Code Audit** (kind `code`) assesses implementation engineering
quality under its separate playbook. Every audit request/report must identify
its kind. For an ambiguous request such as “Please audit X”, the AI must ask
what sort of audit is intended and wait for the answer before starting.
It must not infer the kind, apply a default or silently perform both.

# Project Record Templates

These documents instantiate the planning, control, traceability and assurance layer of [VP's full project quality management system](../../docs/how-vp-works.md). They record actual project authority, work and evidence; template examples themselves are not operational history.

Use with the [standard](../../standards/project-records.md) and
[playbook](../../playbooks/project-records.md). Copy project-view templates
into the chosen root, normally `vp/`. Copy operation templates to
`records/<type-directory>/<ID>/record.md`. Replace every angle-bracket
placeholder; leave no blank required fields. Use `not applicable — reason`
when a field genuinely does not apply. Placeholders are not valid records.

Reserve an ID in the ledger before acting. Fill pre-action sections first.
Append dated amendments to open records; never overwrite pre-action criteria.
Seal terminal outcomes and use new events for subsequent corrections.
Validity is derived from evidence, deadlines, dependencies and later events;
a completed record alone does not make a claim current.
